teams.heading: Jake White names Nathan Hughes, ex-England No. 8, for France clash
teams.body: Fiji-born number eight Nathan Hughes, 35, won 22 caps for England between 2016 and 2019 and returns for Saturday's test against France in Lyon. Hughes qualifies under World Rugby's revised Regulation 8, which allows allegiance switches after a three-year absence from a previous national team with a birthright connection and World Rugby approval. He forms a loose trio with Pita-Gus Sowakula and Kitione Salawa, the second game of Jake White's tenure.

lead.why: A fresh Fiji selection call, with a named former England international and a numbered team sheet, is the story a fan would text about.

teams.heading: Tom Curry major injury doubt for Australia Test, Ben Curry in line
teams.body: Tom Curry is understood to have pulled up injured during Wednesday's full-bore training session, and the nature of the problem has not been disclosed. Fears remain he could miss the whole November campaign, a blow after Guy Pepper and Sam Underhill were already sidelined. Borthwick names his team later on Friday, with twin brother Ben, who has not played for England since 2025, under strong consideration for No. 7.

lead.why: A fresh injury doubt to a key England back-rower, two days before the Australia Test, with a selection call due today.

teams.heading: Galthié names Gourgues first start as Dupont captains injury-hit France against Fiji
teams.body: Les Bleus open their European leg against Fiji in Lyon on Saturday without Meafou, Flament, Jalibert, Brau-Boirie and Thomas Ramos, and Oscar Jegou was ruled out with a rib injury picked up in training. Dupont captains the side from number nine, ousting Maxime Lucu to the bench, and Kalvin Gourgues makes his first start after four appearances off the bench. Théo Attissogbe covers full-back for Ramos, and Esteban Capilla is set to make his Test debut from the replacements.

lead.why: It is a new France selection event with a named matchday 23, and it is the freshest France item on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Sean Jansen starts at No. 8 for Ireland with Doris, Conan sidelined
teams.body: Connacht back-rower Sean Jansen gets a run of starts this month after injuries to Caelan Doris and Jack Conan opened the No. 8 shirt. The New Zealand-born forward made his Ireland debut against Japan in July, and his man-of-the-match display earned him a bench spot against the All Blacks in Auckland. "I'm not just here to fill a jersey because a few boys are injured," he says.

lead.why: A fresh selection story with concrete facts: an injury-driven start at No. 8 and a debut-to-bench route for a player the pack names.

teams.heading: Quesada rests Fischetti, moves Capuozzo to wing for Springboks clash
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada has moved Danilo Fischetti to the bench after six consecutive starts, judging that four more in a row would be too much. Alessandro Fusco gets the nod at scrum-half over Stephen Varney, who has been travelling back and forth from England. Ange Capuozzo shifts to the right wing after limited time training with the squad, and Domingo Miotti, newly joined, is not expected to play against South Africa or in the Argentina match that follows, Quesada said at the team announcement.

lead.why: It is the freshest squad-selection event on the shortlist, and Quesada's own explanation of the team gives it concrete Italy-side facts.

teams.heading: Jeff Wilson says only bizarre officiating can stop All Blacks against Scotland
teams.body: All Blacks great Jeff Wilson is 'pretty confident' New Zealand can go through November unbeaten, and the only thing he can see derailing them at Murrayfield on Saturday is officiating. Scotland have never beaten the All Blacks, yet in 2025 they trailed 17-0 before a McKenzie cameo gave the visitors a 25-17 win. Wilson also credits the injuries with widening the squad and keeping players fresher.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy defends naming record nine England-based players for Japan
teams.body: Wales must embrace picking England-based players, Steve Tandy insists, after naming a record nine of them in the starting XV for Saturday's Nations Championship clash with Japan. "Ultimately it doesn't matter where they play, it'll be the best players selected," said the Wales boss. He argues the players are in demand and performing well in those environments. Only six England-based players were in the 33-strong squad at the 2023 World Cup.

lead.why: A fresh Wales story with a sourced coach quote, and it is separate from the midfield selection already covered this week.

teams.heading: Contepomi shuffles 12 Pumas starters, recalling Juan Cruz Mallia for Ireland
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has made 12 changes to the Argentina team for Friday's Nations Championship test against Ireland, the lineup following the 28-28 draw with Australia in September. The headline call is fullback Juan Cruz Mallia, who returns for the first time in almost a year after ruptured knee ligaments from a late tackle by England's Tom Curry. Contepomi wants a more polished unit across three Tests, against Ireland, Italy and France, and says discipline will be key after Argentina were reduced to 13 men late against Australia.

lead.why: A fresh, concrete selection story about Argentina's own XV, with the return of a key fullback from a long injury layoff.

teams.heading: Rugby Australia sends pay offer directly to Wallabies, bypassing players' union
teams.body: The pay talks are now being fought in public, with the governing body writing to players this week to spell out its terms. The letter went around the Rugby Union Players' Association, which handles negotiations. Rupa president Tom Robertson voiced disappointment at the timing, "particularly while the Wallabies are on tour." RA chair Daniel Herbert said Rupa's counter-proposals "threaten the future of the game in Australia." The previous agreement, struck in 2023, ran through the two Bledisloe Cup defeats to New Zealand.

lead.why: A new, fresh dispute over the Wallabies' own pay talks, with on-record statements from both sides, and it is Australia's story rather than England's.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones drafts in former Wales flanker Kingsley Jones for Cardiff
teams.body: Kingsley Jones, the former Wales flanker who left Canada's head coaching job last year, has spent the week in Japan's camp ahead of Saturday's match in Cardiff. Japan's head coach says the role is simple: "He's in camp, just watching what we're doing and feeding back on how we can improve." Eddie Jones also admits he already has a very good idea of how Wales will play, and Japan are still chasing a first win on Welsh soil.

lead.why: It is a new item about Japan's own camp, with a named coach, a named staff addition and a coach's on-record comment, and it has the most corroboration of the shortlist.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie says hip-drop tackles will be refereed strongly after London talks
teams.body: Rennie named his team for Saturday's match against Scotland and used the press conference to report on World Rugby's London meeting with Test coaches. The main topic was the hip-drop and knee-drop tackles, both recently outlawed, and he said the hip drop had never been discussed before. "From a safety point of view, it'll be refereed strongly." On the brake foot, Rennie said referees have a clear process, and he does not expect much change before the World Cup.

lead.why: Rennie's post-team-naming briefing gave the first new, on-record New Zealand account of the World Rugby London meeting and how hip-drop tackles will be policed.

teams.heading: Ruan Nortje backs Salmaan Moerat as Etzebeth's replacement for Italy
teams.body: Moerat gets the nod at lock because Eben Etzebeth is sidelined with a leg injury and has not been included in the squad for the Nations Championship Tests in Europe. Moerat, who has captained the Boks in four of his 11 Tests, is ahead of Lood de Jager, Franco Mostert and uncapped Riley Norton. Nortje and Moerat go back to 2017 and played together for the Junior Boks, and Nortje says every game alongside him is "a real honour."

lead.why: A fresh squad-selection story about South Africa's own second row, replacing the injured Etzebeth, which beats the club transfers and the Italian-side items.
